newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-SOCCER PROMOTION BATTLE DELAYS ATHLETICS.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-SOCCER PROMOTION BATTLE DELAYS ATHLETICS.

text.p: A strong Algerian squad opened their Mediterranean Games campaign on Sunday with a victory by Azzedine Sakhri in the men's marathon but an Italian soccer match delayed other athletics events by 24 hours.
Sakhri won the men's marathon along the coastline of this southern town in two hours 20 minutes 40 seconds. Giovanni Ruggiero of Italy took silver and Morocco's Mustapha Damaoui won bronze.
Confusion emerged over the start of other track finals in Bari's San Nicola stadium because of a second division soccer match there on Sunday between Bari and Castel di Sangro.
First scheduled for Sunday, the finals were put back a day.

Organisational problems and a depleted line-up have fuelled concern that the Mediterranean Games, held every four years, have little importance in a crowded athletics calendar leading up to August's world championships in Athens.
The Algerians are fielding the strongest squad. Hassiba Boulmerka, the 1,500 metres Olympic champion in 1992, is one of the major attractions in the women's athletics.
The competition is missing British-born Italian long jumper Fiona May, who took silver at the Atlanta Olympics, and many of the Moroccan 5,000 and 10,000 metres specialists.
A notable absentee from the French squad is Olympic 200 metres champion Marie-Jose Perec.
Twenty-one countries from around the Mediterranean are competing in 27 disciplines at the Games.
